common: An original Roman-era elemental-mage prison game, drawn digitally by hand as a complete two-dimensional illustration. Roman-inspired tunics, sandals, limewashed masonry, terracotta, bronze collars and ward stones; invented people and symbols only. Entire scene in focus, clear silhouettes, readable at a reduced game-screen scale. No three-dimensional rendering, photography, modern equipment, existing franchise designs, text, letters, numbers, logos, watermark, panel grid or decorative outer frame.

scenes.arena: Draw an overhead tactical action-RPG fight on a broad sandy Roman arena floor, with small foreshortened combatants seen from above, open paths between them, and a thin rim of stone wall at the screen edges. At lower centre a Water mage faces straight UP the screen with both hands reaching toward enemies: immediately ABOVE her head is an inverted-U cyan magical shield arc, opening DOWN toward her, protecting her front while the sand BELOW and BEHIND her is completely bare. An orange fireball from the enemy mage at upper right bursts into a compact white spark on the TOP edge of this cyan shield arc; separately, a thin cyan needle from the player's outstretched hand travels diagonally toward a shield-bearing soldier at upper left. A slinger farther left and a cinder hound to the right create spaced threats, with a small jagged red-and-black warning patch off to the right; each fighter is small within the broad overhead floor, and every effect has its own clearly readable path. All figures, spell marks and terrain are hand-painted parts of this single game-view illustration; leave quiet strips along the top and bottom for later interface labels.
scenes.camp: A wide overhead illustrated navigation map of the guarded mage camp, a complete walkable enclosure with branching paths and small collared adult inhabitants, no combat or spellcasting. Arrange a staff-training yard at upper left, a dry round cistern at upper centre, a sunken sparring pit at upper right; a market of awnings at middle left, a communal bread table and gathering square at the centre, a monumental barred arena door at middle right; a cluster of patched living tents at lower left, and a fogbound camp boundary with a secluded meeting path at lower right. Make each destination a distinct recognizable landmark with empty ground nearby for later code-drawn labels; salt ward posts and patrolling guards communicate confinement without obscuring routes. Leave calm space along the top for the day time-slot strip and along the bottom for destination information; draw only the map, all text and time-slot controls are added in code.
